# Pilotage

> Pilotage is an open extension of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for guided
> program authoring and verified execution. Where MCP lets an agent call tools,
> Pilotage lets it safely author and run whole programs (SQL, automation rules,
> workflow documents) against any live system: the server publishes a manifest
> (read at the handshake), guides (the language's grammar), a versioned catalog
> (the live vocabulary), side-effect-free validation with closed diagnostic codes,
> a pre-run plan with per-step risk, and an execution trace with every branch
> decision on the record, riding the execute response, and fetchable later by
> run id if the run was stored. The layers: manifest, guides, catalog,
> validate, plan, execute, trace, with the agent at the center orchestrating. Governing
> rule: standardize the loop, not the language. Extension id: io.github.jafarsa0/pilotage.
> Spec v1.1 · text CC BY 4.0, schemas/vectors/tooling Apache-2.0 · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21396027.

## Specification

- [Spec index](https://pilotagespec.org/SPEC.md): entry point and part map
- [Part I: Story and positioning](https://pilotagespec.org/spec/part-i-story-and-positioning.md): the three problems, the missing layer, related work, why this belongs in MCP
- [Part II: Abstract model](https://pilotagespec.org/spec/part-ii-abstract-model.md): the normative core (actors, capability declarations, the eight shapes, reserved statuses/codes, trace identity, processing order, trust model)
- [Part III: MCP binding](https://pilotagespec.org/spec/part-iii-mcp-binding.md): the manifest tool, loop tools, reserved argument names, error routing, session binding
- [Part IV: Implementation notes](https://pilotagespec.org/spec/part-iv-implementation-notes.md): native vs adapted engines, the both-polarity test method, the completeness gate

## Machine-readable artifacts

- [JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12)](https://pilotagespec.org/schemas/1.1/pilotage.schema.json): every wire shape (manifest, plan, trace, outcome, diagnostics, errors)
- [Conformance vectors](https://pilotagespec.org/conformance/vectors.json): 54 engine-neutral test vectors, both polarities, keyed to spec requirements
- [Conformance harness](https://pilotagespec.org/conformance/README.md): runnable Node harness that executes the vectors against any live server

## Guides (docs that execute, replayed against the live server in CI)

- [Your first verified run](https://pilotagespec.org/guides/01-your-first-verified-run.md): the whole loop once: discover, learn, look up, validate (with the classic typo), execute pinned, fetch the run's trace back by id
- [Drift, risk, and recovery](https://pilotagespec.org/guides/02-drift-risk-and-recovery.md): catalog_drift and re-pinning, the destructive-risk gate, test_run, idempotency, partial outcomes

## Try it live

- Example server endpoint (MCP over HTTP, per-session isolated): POST https://harborview.pilotagespec.org/mcp
- [Harborview source](https://github.com/jafarsa0/harborview): the public example server, a simulated smart building speaking buildingflow/1, Apache-2.0

## Proof (recorded experiment)

- [Proof kit and results](https://github.com/jafarsa0/pilotage/blob/main/proof/README.md): a recorded experiment, run twice: models from three providers complete real work in buildingflow/1, a language in no training data; raw unedited transcripts, a neutral exam, a fact-checking grader
- [Rendered proof page](https://pilotagespec.org/proof.html): the same experiment presented on the website
